description: Extract of a real stored report row, inspected 2026-10-19; not a new benchmark or biological validation.

row.conclusion: 4 SNPs previously reported to be associated with longevity were verified in this study. 4 novel SNPs (rs12206094, rs13220810, rs7762395, and rs9486902 (corrected P-values 0.001–0.044)) and two haplotypes(corrected P-values: 0.01–0.03) associated with longevity were found in this study. FOXO3A was a candidate longevity gene for survival from younger ages to old age, yet not during old age.

studies.study_design: FOXO3A polymorphisms (rs2802292, rs2764264, and rs13217795) were analyzed for longevity associations in 281 long-lived men (age range 90-108 years) and 195 controls (age range 18-48 years) from the Southern Italian Centenarian Study.
studies.conclusion: rs2802288, a proxy of rs2802292, showed the best allelic association--minor allele frequency (MAF) = 0.49; p = 0.003; odds ratio (OR) = 1.51; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.15-1.98).

studies.study_design: Six tagging SNPs from FOXO1A and FOXO3A were selected and genotyped in 1817 centenarians and younger individuals
studies.conclusion: All 3 SNPs of FOXO3A were associated with longevity in both genders (P = 0.005-0.001)

studies.study_design: Nested-case control study of 5 candidate longevity genes in 8006 Japanese American men from the Honolulu Heart Program and 3741 men part of the Honolulu Asia Aging Study
studies.conclusion: Genetic variation in the FOXO3A gene was associated with longevity

studies.study_design: Three SNPs in FOXO1A and three in FOXO3A were analyzed in a sample of 760 centenarians (578 female and 182 male) and 1060 middle-age controls (378 female and 682 male)
studies.conclusion: All three SNPs in FOXO3A were positively associated with longevity in both genders, even at ages 92-110 (odds ratio [OR] = 1.61–1.73, p = .0002–0.005; dominant model)

studies.study_design: 15 SNPs that covered FOXO3A common variation were examined in 1089 oldest old and 736 middle-aged for longevity association by longitudinal study design as well as case-control study design
studies.conclusion: 4 SNPs previously reported to be associated with longevity were verified in this study. 4 novel SNPs (rs12206094, rs13220810, rs7762395, and rs9486902 (corrected P-values 0.001–0.044)) and two haplotypes(corrected P-values: 0.01–0.03) associated with longevity were found in this study. FOXO3A was a candidate longevity gene for survival from younger ages to old age, yet not during old age.
